subject: Status - reverse substitution works, ambiguity is where we lose
body:
Status.

Reverse substitution is running and the dictionary covers 612 acronyms across the three pilot teams, which is more than I expected Amara to get in a month.

Model results on our internal snippet set (287 snippets, hand-written, roughly the size of the clinician set in the release): 88% expansion accuracy overall. But that number hides the split. Unambiguous acronyms - one expansion in the dictionary - are at 96%. Ambiguous ones, where the same three letters mean different things in platform vs support vs finance, are at 61%.

That's not a model problem so much as a context problem: the snippets often don't contain enough signal to disambiguate, and neither would a human without knowing which team wrote the ticket. Adding the authoring team as a feature took ambiguous accuracy to 79% in a quick test.

Recommendation: make team-context a required input rather than pretending we can do this from text alone.

Halima
